title: Base Salary Calculator: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay (38-Hour Week, Fortnight & Year)
description: Use our base salary calculator to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay. Based on a 38-hour week, 52-week year, including tax and super.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary using the base salary calculator?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. Our base salary calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week, so annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual pay is about $52,269 before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the base salary calculator include casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes, you can add 25% casual loading using the checkbox. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The calculator adds the loading on top of your base hourly rate. For the minimum wage, casual loading gives $33.05 per hour, annual gross about $65,336.

faqs.q: How is superannuation treated in the base salary calculator?
faqs.a: Super is estimated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator shows super separately; it is not deducted from your take-home pay. Tax and Medicare are estimated using the 2026–27 resident rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Use the Base Salary Calculator to Understand Your Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your current hourly rate, the [base salary calculator](/topics/hourly-conversion) helps you see the full picture. It converts your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly and weekly figures, assuming a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year. This is the most common full-time arrangement in Australia under the Fair Work system.

### How the Calculation Works

The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours every week, that's hourly × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay. The calculator also shows your fortnightly pay (weekly × 2) and weekly pay. If you work different hours, you can adjust the hours per week field.

### What About Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage?

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. Many employees are covered by awards that set higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The [pay guides](/blog) on our site list award-specific rates. Remember, the National Minimum Wage is a minimum, not a median or average for any job.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. Our calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the calculator add it. For example, the casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25).

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). It is not deducted from your salary; it's an extra contribution from your employer. The calculator shows an estimated super amount, but it stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For most workers, super adds significantly to your total remuneration.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

The calculator estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page explains these deductions in more detail. Note that this is an estimate – it assumes you claim the full tax-free threshold and no other offsets. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included.

### What the Calculator Does Not Cover

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using the Calculator for Salary Negotiation

If you have a salary offer, you can work backwards to find the equivalent hourly rate. Divide the annual salary by 1,976 (38 × 52) to get the hourly rate before tax and super. For example, an offer of $80,000 per year gives about $40.49 per hour. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page shows that ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026 – that's an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. The calculator shows your fortnightly gross pay (weekly × 2). For a minimum wage full-time worker, that's about $2,009.80 before tax. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing to advertised salaries that are often quoted annually.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act. The 52-week year is used because most employees work year-round, though some industries have school-holiday breaks or seasonal shutdowns. If your work pattern differs, adjust the hours per week in the calculator.

### Check Your Award or Agreement

Your actual pay may be higher than the minimum if you are covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Use the [reference tables](/data) to find the correct classification rate. The base salary calculator is a starting point – always check your pay slip and your award for penalty rates, allowances, and overtime.

### Summary

The base salary calculator is a practical tool for understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay. It uses the standard 38-hour week and 52-week year, includes casual loading and super, and estimates tax and Medicare. Remember that it provides an estimate only. For your exact pay and tax situation, consult your employer, payroll, or the Australian Taxation Office.
